- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.4) — model is overly cautious, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent price drops or sentiment shifts — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves — reduce forecast magnitude after large spikes or drops.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early sessions (e.g., first 5–7 days) — dampen initial forecast peaks if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.7–0.9), add 2–5% to forecast; if falling (0.3–0.5), subtract 2–5% — adjust based on sentiment slope, not absolute value.
